newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe police use force to stop protesters.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe police use force to stop protesters.

text.p: Zimbabwean riot police on Monday broke up a planned protest march by trade unions, human rights groups and churches in support of striking medical workers.

About 50 police pounced without warning on 200 people who had gathered at the Harare magistrate court building in preparation for a march into the city centre, firing teargas and beating them with baton sticks.
Scores of other people who were streaming to join the crowd fled, with some -- choking and tears running down their cheeks -- rushing into the magistrate court building as the police gave chase.
Witnesses said police arrested Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU) secretary-general Morgan Tsvangirayi and his vice president Isaac Matongo.
ZCTU national organising secretary James Makore, who was with the crowd, slammed the use of force to break up the crowd as unneccessary.
"They didn't warn us at all. They just fired teargas and they were actually firing directly at people. They didn't have to use such strong-arm tactics," he told reporters.
Dozens more riot police cordoned off the campuses of Harare's University of Zimbabwe and the Polytechnical College to stop students from joining the planned march.
Makore said the ZCTU would meet later with other organisers of the planned march: "The best thing will be to assemble the leadership because we have to restrategise to find out exactly what to do."

The march was called by the ZCTU, the Public Service Association, the main national human rights watchdog Zimrights and the Zimbabwe Council of Churches to press the government to resolve a strike by nurses and junior doctors that has hit public hospitals countrywide.
"What we are saying is the government should quicken the process of resolving this crisis because people are dying," Makore said.
The government of President Robert Mugabe has taken a hardline against the strikers, saying they are fired.
On Monday, acting Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare Minister Nathan Shamuyarira told state media the government would not back down.
He disputed statements by authorities in the country's largest hospitals, Parirenyatwa and Harare, that they had closed due to the strike, saying only a few wards were not operating.
Union officials say 10,000 of 14,000 nurses employed in state hospitals and 500 of 800 doctors are on strike but Shamuyarira said on Monday only 1,000 nurses and 100 doctors were involved.
